slot.subtopic: Diagonal relationship of Li and Mg
slot.brief: Which statement about the Li–Mg diagonal relationship is correct/incorrect (similar ionic size, nitride formation, carbonate decomposition)?

stem: Which statement correctly describes a similarity between lithium and magnesium arising from their diagonal relationship?
options: Both form nitrides by direct combination with nitrogen.
Both form thermally stable carbonates that do not decompose on heating.
Both form nitrates that give nitrites on heating.

verdicts.working: Lithium and magnesium both combine directly with nitrogen to form nitrides: Li₃N and Mg₃N₂. The other statements are false: their carbonates decompose on heating, their nitrates form oxides rather than nitrites, and their bicarbonates are not stable solids.

working:
Lithium and magnesium both combine directly with nitrogen to form nitrides: $6\text{Li}+\text{N}_2\rightarrow2\text{Li}_3\text{N}$; $3\text{Mg}+\text{N}_2\rightarrow\text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2$.

Independent check: Lithium and magnesium both combine directly with nitrogen to form nitrides: Li₃N and Mg₃N₂. The other statements are false: their carbonates decompose on heating, their nitrates form oxides rather than nitrites, and their bicarbonates are not stable solids.
solution:
Lithium and magnesium both combine directly with nitrogen to form nitrides:
$$6\text{Li}+\text{N}_2\rightarrow2\text{Li}_3\text{N},\qquad 3\text{Mg}+\text{N}_2\rightarrow\text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2.$$
